[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Agnes was born in 1658. She is the daughter of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-460|Helen Clerk]].

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3077]] is assessed at 78% (probable). Agnes's 15 August 1658 St Cuthbert's baptism index names James Glesgow and Helen Clerk. The same James name and St Cuthbert’s locality, with the 1658 child just before the 1661–65 Annapill household, support a possible earlier partnership in one father’s life.

Probable combined identification, not an equation of Helen Clerk with Annapill. The separate mothers and earlier birth/date attribution remain qualified; a second James is possible.

Next useful test: Compare the two couples’ marriage/residence records and the original 1658 entry.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F318-T2H "Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F318-T2H : 16 September 2021), James Glesgow in entry for Agnes Glesgow, 1658.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


A possible identification concerns Agnes Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Agnes Glasgow and Patrik Paul on 8 July 1670 at Kirknewton and East Calder.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 690/10 / 64; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.

A possible identification concerns Agnes Glasgow. The banns/marriage index records Agnes Glasgow and William Thomsone on 15 December 1681 at Carstairs.<ref>Scotland’s People: Old Parish Registers — banns and marriages: OPR 633/10 / 66; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ record].</ref> The original parish register image has not been inspected. The combined index date does not by itself identify the precise event type. The identification remains uncertain.
